messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Let's run the postmortem for last night's notification backlog. @lead walk us through the timeline.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Timeline: at 23:10 the send queue depth started climbing; by 23:40 we were three hours behind.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: I pulled the upstream logs. The provider throttled us, but our retry loop made it worse.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: I believe the upstream cap is 200 requests per second, so the throttling is surprising.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Actually the provider's log evidence shows the contractual cap is 100 requests per second. We were sending at 180.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Good catch. So the cap is 100 requests per second and our retry loop tripled the pressure.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Root cause: our retry policy had no backoff jitter, so retries synchronized and stacked on top of the limit.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Confirmed: adding jitter alone cut upstream errors by 70% in replay.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Lesson: retries toward a rate-limited upstream must always include jitter. Write that down.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Recorded. I will add it to the integration checklist.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: @lead please record this as a project rule: every external integration must document its rate limit in the service registry.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Recorded: every external integration must document its rate limit in the service registry.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: I propose we stop retrying provider 429 responses inline, and requeue them with a delay instead.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Agreed: on 429 we requeue with a 30 second delay instead of inline retry.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: One number to verify for the report: I think the incident ran about 100 minutes.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Verified from the logs: the incident window was 82 minutes.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Good, 82 minutes it is.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Separately: I propose we page on queue depth, not only on error rate.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Agreed: queue depth over 10k becomes a paging alert.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Preference note for postmortems: keep them blameless, and give every action item a calendar date.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Understood, blameless with dated action items.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: If we had shipped the jitter fix a week earlier, this outage would not have happened.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Counterfactuals do not help; let's keep the document factual.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: What is our target for normal queue depth?

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Baseline is under 2k; the 10k number is the alerting line.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: OK. The postmortem goes out tomorrow with the dated action items.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: I will draft it tonight and attach the replay evidence.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: I will attach the upstream error charts.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Name the doc with the incident date, like inc_2026-10-01_queue_backlog.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Done, following that naming.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Also scheduling a follow-up review in two weeks.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Thanks everyone.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Great session.
